issues.description: The problem statement repeatedly refers to a method named printFarmSong(), but both the template and solution implementations use singFarmSong() as the public method that plays the song. This name mismatch between the specification and the code can confuse students about which method to implement or call and may cause them to implement the wrong method name.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the names across artifacts. Either update the problem statement to instruct students to implement singFarmSong() (and refer to singFarmSongVerse() accordingly), or change the template and solution to expose a public printFarmSong() method (which delegates to the existing singFarmSong() implementation) so that the specification and code match.

issues.description: The problem statement (UML and task text) refers to a Farm method named printFarmSong(), but both the template and the solution implement and reference a method named singFarmSong(). This mismatches the identifier students are asked to implement vs. the starter code and reference implementation, creating confusion about which method name to use and where to place the song-printing logic.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the method name consistent across artifacts. Either update the problem statement and UML to refer to singFarmSong(), or rename the method in the template and solution to printFarmSong() (and update any calls such as in Main) so all three artifacts use the same identifier.
